text:
Marathon Petroleum stock inched up 0.24% today after rallying 13.2% over two weeks, riding a sharp climb in oil prices. U.S. crude jumped above $101 a barrel today following Iranian escalation in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping chokepoint for global oil — and Brent crude hit $110, reflecting the added premium buyers pay when supply routes face disruption. For a refiner, higher crude prices can pinch margins in the short term, but the company is also benefiting from elevated fuel prices and refinery utilization at 93.5%, near full capacity, which keeps throughput strong.

The broader tailwind is that global oil tightness is real: tanker rates have surged enough that the "true" cost to deliver physical oil is roughly $38 a barrel above the headline price, and refineries are running hot to meet demand amid geopolitical supply concerns. That structural strength in energy markets—not any company-specific news today—is what's driven the two-week gain.
